# Independent audit: nonsimplex bipyramid cap germs and affine descent

Source: `candidate b34a13272d68f2d8`.

**Result: PASS.** The author applied the sole requested wording repair:
Section 3 now calls B a compact convex body in R^n, with the n=0 singleton
convention. This ensures C_0 has interior in the claimed ambient space.
No mathematical repair to the cap, depth, or ownership arguments is needed.

The source verifier passes 126 exact checks. The independent verifier
`supporting computation verify_nonsimplex_bipyramid_audit_slab_recovery.py` passes 6,184 exact
checks, supplementing the following classical audit. These finite checks
are not used as a proof in unrestricted dimensions.

## 1. Body, measure, and baseline continuous bound

The double pyramid is the convex hull of the embedded simplex and its two
tips. Its volume is 2 V_p/(p+1), and its centroid is zero by the simplex
slice centroids and reflection in t. Each of its p+3 listed vertices is
exposed, so it is not a d-simplex when d=p+1. The integer fibers in Section
3 are full d-dimensional positive homothetic copies, hence q=d and the
Hausdorff measure is exactly the finite sum of their d-volumes.

The input `candidate 732b11a769399016` states
and proves the required paired inequality in every simplex dimension p,
with all threshold statuses. Its dimension parameter is p here, not d.
Pairing t and -t produces precisely the two opposite pairs
(h-vt,-h+vt) and (-h-vt,h+vt). Their total bound integrates to 2 delta V.
For u=0, the nonatomic symmetric t-marginal instead gives V, strictly
larger than 2 delta V because p>=2. This treats vertical normals too.

The canonical continuous caps all cost delta V and their normals sum to
zero; they cover the entire ambient space. Thus they give both the lower
and upper bounds needed for the exact ordinary maximum delta V.

## 2. Complete baseline critical menu

If u is not an ordinary minimizing simplex direction, at slice t=0 the
paired slice cost strictly exceeds its paired lower bound. Continuity in
t preserves a positive strict gap on an interval; outside it the input
paired inequality prevents cancellation. The classical simplex equality
case therefore restricts u to a positive canonical normal.

For a canonical direction, a nonzero opposite displacement s has strict
paired surplus. When both simplex cuts are proper this follows from
strict convexity of the degree-p power; once one cut is full it alone
exceeds twice the lower bound. A nonzero vertical coefficient v yields
such a displacement on every slice with t>0 and positive radius. Thus
v=0 is necessary. This argument includes the two tips on the critical
boundary: it does not use a fictitious whole-body smooth vertex chamber.

The same argument shows strict paired surplus for a nonzero common
threshold h on K_p, which is exactly the fact subsequently needed to
eliminate integer tilts on reflected equal fibers. No stronger strictness
for arbitrary noncanonical shifted pairs is used.

## 3. Cap formula and all statuses

For h>=0, proper slices have radius rho>=h/p and cap volume
 delta V_p (rho-h/p)^p. Integrating gives delta V(r-h/p)^d.
For h=-q in [-r,0], rho<=q is fully captured, while rho>=q has the
proper cap formula. The correction coefficient is exactly

    1-delta*((p+1)/p)^d = -1/p,

since d=p+1. Thus the source formula includes the negative correction
-(V/p)(-h)_+^d. At h=-r it gives the whole volume V r^d; at h=pr it gives
zero. At h=0 the correction and its first derivative vanish (d>=3).
The cap formulas for all canonical normals agree by simplex symmetry.

## 4. Baseline global sources and their strict gaps

Equal reflected fibers see opposite thresholds in every through-middle
ambient cap, so their paired bounds and the own-fiber ordinary bound
sum to Q_0. Pure integer caps capture at least half the total mass and
are strictly more expensive. Canonical cylinders attain Q_0 and cover
all points in every fiber, proving the GLOBAL upper bound as well.
The own positive fiber forces a canonical continuous normal in any
minimizer; strict reflected-pair surplus then forces every integer
evaluation to vanish. Integer normals in span(P)^perp have no effect
and are correctly treated as the same trace.

The full simplex permutation group, together with t-reflection, preserves
every radial family, volume, and the integer base. Its orbit average in
each continuous fiber is zero. Convexity of depth superlevel sets hence
makes every fiber centroid a fiber maximum, without replacing its source
by an averaged point outside the actual fiber.

At a nonzero source base z_0, the derivative of the canonical tilted cap
is exactly -(delta V d/p) z_0 sum r_z^(d-1). Choosing the perturbation
along z_0 strictly lowers its mass. Finite P gives a positive minimum of
these finitely many strict centroid gaps. No global formula for the
perturbed middle depth is needed to preserve this comparison.

For a middle point with nonzero equatorial coordinate, one canonical
cap shifted through that point strictly loses own-fiber mass. For a
point (0,t_0), the displayed vertical perturbation has derivative

    -t_0*(2 delta V_p/p)*sum r_z^p.

The sign and factor agree with differentiation of the sliced simplex cap:
its threshold derivative at zero is -delta V_p rho^(p-1). The moving
threshold contributes (t-t_0), whose odd part integrates to zero, while
integral rho^(p-1)dt=2r^p/p. A global threshold-Lipschitz bound of order
rho^(p-1), multiplied by |t-t_0|, is integrable. This verifies the DCT
step even at the two tip contacts. The baseline source is unique.

## 5. Perturbation and actual cap ownership

Positive concavity survives the affine radius perturbation on the whole
projection, so the fibers are induced by an actual convex body. In the
cap u_i.x-p a.z>=0 its threshold h=p a.z makes r_a-h/p=r^0 exactly.
Summing the correction yields

    Q(a)=Q_0 - V p^(d-1) sum (-a.z)_+^d.

For nonzero a in span(P), symmetry supplies a negative nonzero evaluation,
so Q(a)<Q_0. Pairwise strict convexity of s^d gives M(a)>M_0.

The main cap family covers its owned middle fiber. At every other base,
finite-tilt attainment follows from Section 2 of the earlier arbitrary-rank
source: its polyhedral bounded representative proof is dimension-free,
and continuity uses nonzero continuous normals against d-volume. Pure
integer caps cannot minimize at an interior centroid. Taking the finite
symmetry orbit of one attained cap gives equal masses and zero sum of
continuous normals, hence exact coverage of its owned fiber. Global
coverage is the union of these owned groups, not a claim that each group
covers all bases.

The radial symmetric-difference bound is uniform over ALL halfspaces;
it preserves the strict slack of the frozen auxiliary groups and the
strict other-source gap. Every point belongs to a cap of mass at most
Q(a), yielding actual global depth at most Q(a). The middle centroid is
an actual maximizer by symmetry and the preserved source comparison.
Reselecting critical groups is legitimate, but the source appropriately
does not claim the displayed moved caps themselves remain minimizing.
Scaling uses the d-dimensional Jacobian and gives the stated strict
budget-feasible volume improvement, with an upper bound on depth rather
than an invented equality.

## 6. Explicit three-fiber range

For p=2, V=3 and delta=4/9. Formula (3) gives Q(a)=4-12|a|^3 and
M(a)=9+18a^2 exactly. For |a|<=1/5 every displayed threshold is inside
the allowed cap-formula range. At either exposed integer endpoint, a
finite tilt isolates each own ordinary cap; coefficients of magnitude
10 strictly empty every other displayed fiber throughout this range.
Thus its actual maximum depth is precisely (4/3)(1+/-a)^3, and its
canonical three-cap group is genuinely critical there.

At the middle centroid, the two common centered copies (1-s)K_2 give
paired contribution at least (8/3)(1-s)^3 for every nonvertical ambient
normal; pure integer normals give an even larger bound. The own fiber
contributes at least 4/3. The difference from the largest endpoint depth
is (4/3)(2-9s+3s^2-3s^3), which is positive throughout [0,1/5] and has
unscaled minimum 37/125. Symmetry controls every other point of all
three fibers, so this is an all-source comparison.

At s=1/5 the total mass is 243/25, the displayed upper depth is 488/125,
and the source lower depth is 1012/375. Their normalized values are
488/1215<4/9 and 1012/3645>27/128 respectively. Thus the claimed strict
descent is exact, while its entire certified calibration stays above the
OC target. The note makes no counterexample or arbitrary-fiber claim.
